name: Michaelmas
description: The archangel Michael and the service of angels.
biblicalBasis: Michael fights against the dragon: "A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels went to war against the dragon" (Rev 12:7-12). Daniel 10:13 and 12:1 speak of Michael as the great prince who stands up for the people. Jacob's dream of a ladder between earth and heaven with angels going up and down (Gen 28:12). Jesus' words: "See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for their angels in heaven always see the face of my heavenly Father" (Matt 18:10). Hebrews 1:14 about angels as ministering spirits.
significance: Angels testify that reality is greater than what can be seen. Michael represents God's battle against evil—a battle already won, yet still unfolding. The angels in the Bible are not cute figures but powerful messengers who often say "Do not fear!" They serve God by protecting, guiding, and proclaiming.
liturgicalContext: White color. Celebrated on September 29. In the Lutheran tradition, the day of Michael and all angels is celebrated—not Michael alone. In folk tradition, Michaelmas marked the end of summer and the beginning of autumn.
history: The celebration on September 29 dates back to the 400s–500s, originally linked to the dedication of a church of Michael in Rome. In the Middle Ages, Michaelmas was one of the major annual festivals with markets and accounting settlements. The cult of Michael was strong throughout Europe.
otConnections: Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12)—angels as mediators between heaven and earth. Balaam's donkey seeing the angel that humans cannot see (Num 22:21-35). The angel guarding the way to the tree of life (Gen 3:24). The seraphim in Isaiah's temple vision (Isa 6). Angels accompanying Israel through the wilderness (Exod 23:20).

references.reason: The day is dedicated to the archangel Michael and the service of angels. Matthew 18:10 is the central biblical text for this day in the church year, where Jesus confirms that the little ones have angels who see God's face. This is an explicit and unique connection.
